source.title: Beyond the Covariance Trap: Unlocking Generalization in Same-Subject Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models
source.authors: Xiyu Liu; Qing-Yi Si; Zhengxiao Liu; Chenxu Yang; Nai-Bin Gu; Zheng Lin

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures instruction-following after deliberate same-subject knowledge editing. That induced behavior does not test whether standard training on natural labels generalizes, or any of V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on instruction-following and prompt-form generalization after knowledge editing. Those findings concern an edited model and do not test the claim versions about standard training, memorization, architecture, optimization, regularization, sharpness–gap correlations in ordinarily trained networks, or memorized training examples.
record.test_reason: The study measures recall across prompt forms after deliberate factual edits to instruction-tuned LLMs. None of V1–V8 names this behavior or intervention. Its tolerance radius measures activation-space robustness, not magnitude-aware weight sharpness or its correlation with training–test gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they attribute same-subject editing failures under instructions to activation deviation exceeding edited-value tolerance, and propose RoSE to reduce deviation and expand tolerance. These are the authors' mechanistic interpretations, not evidence for V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The study edits existing instruction-tuned LLMs using locate-then-edit methods; it does not train networks on natural or random labels using standard gradient methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differences by model, editing method, layer, prompt form, and number of sequential edits. It reports that the tolerance radius varies by model and edit setting, and that the covariance-based versus identity-based update changes activation deviation.

fits_no_version.finding: RoSE improves instructed-query efficacy and paraphrase scores over MEMIT-Merge on S2RKE across the three evaluated model sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Knowledge editors differ in how reliably edited facts are recalled across held-out prompt forms.

fits_no_version.finding: Joint same-subject edits have smaller activation-space tolerance radii than isolated edits. Identity-based updates reduce activation deviation, although the Llama deviation still exceeds its joint-edit radius without HKI.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Same-subject editing robustness depends on edited-value noise tolerance and prompt-induced activation deviation.

fits_no_version.finding: Different relations for one subject have near-orthogonal editing gradients in the two probed models; the authors attribute reduced tolerance to this geometry.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Joint factual editing involves near-orthogonal relation gradients associated with reduced edited-value tolerance.

record.problems: The paper's findings are specific to deliberately edited knowledge and instruction or prompt-form recall, so they do not establish the catalog claim about ordinary training on natural labels. Several geometric results are figure-based with only approximate values stated in text. The authors report experiments on two 7B/8B instruction models for the main benchmarks; broader model-size evidence is limited to the reported 14B evaluation and key-similarity analysis.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were retained for LoCoMo-Edit table metrics, locality metrics, individual baseline methods, ablation conditions, sequential edits, or layer sensitivity figures. Those results concern editing performance, locality, resource use, or sensitivity rather than any V1–V8 measure; included rows summarize the directly relevant edited-model prompt-form results and geometric measures.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover held-out performance.
Dropout effects on classifier test error across training-set sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness ranking training–test gaps among comparably fitted convolutional networks, including comparisons against norm and margin measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because none measures a named version; this does not imply the reported editing effects are absent. No additional version-bearing results appear in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under standard training.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold in ordinarily trained networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers trained from scratch.
Generalization differences between adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers under the stated tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Effects of dropout and its removal with data augmentation in ordinarily trained classifiers.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness ranks training–test gaps in ordinarily trained networks.
Effects of removing memorized training examples and retraining on test accuracy.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured tolerance radius R for isolated MEMIT edits versus joint same-subject MEMIT-Merge edits.
rows.note: The measured radius concerns robustness of the edited value vector to noise, not the training–test gap in the claim.
rows.check: The reported 92.9 versus 23.3 measures robustness to noise added to edited value vectors; it cannot establish any claim version.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured activation deviation under standard covariance-based and identity-based updates.
rows.note: Covariance update exceeds the edited-model tolerance radius; identity update lowers the deviation below it. This is prompt-form robustness after editing.
rows.check: Activation deviation does not measure any version. For this comparison, covariance-based D ≈ 26.1 is the baseline and identity-based D ≈ 17.4 is the result; R ≈ 23.3 is a separate reference measure.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured tolerance radius R for isolated MEMIT edits versus joint same-subject MEMIT-Merge edits.
rows.note: The paper reports this as a collapse in tolerance for edited values.
rows.check: The reported 10.2 versus 1.7 concerns noise tolerance of edited activations, not any version's generalization measure.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured activation deviation under standard covariance-based and identity-based updates.
rows.value: D ≈ 2.6 with covariance; D ≈ 2.2 with identity; R ≈ 1.7
rows.note: Both deviations exceed the reported joint-edit tolerance radius; identity reduces deviation but does not bring it below the radius in this result.
rows.check: Activation deviation does not measure any version. Covariance-based D ≈ 2.6 is the baseline and identity-based D ≈ 2.2 is the result; both exceed R ≈ 1.7. Figure 10's caption suggests a below-radius result, contradicting these numerical statements.
